newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to send 400 peacekeepers to Albania force.
newsitem.headline: Romania to send 400 peacekeepers to Albania force.

text.p: Romania, keen to boost its chances of early admission to NATO, will dispatch 400 troops as part of the Italian-led multinational force aimed to protect aid to chaos-torn Albania, defence officials said on Monday.

"Romania's decision to join this mission is a political test for our country's capacity to become a NATO member," state news agency Rompres quoted army chief of staff General Constantin Degeratu as saying.
Romania wants to carve a role for itself as a pole of stability in the volatile Balkans. The new Bucharest leaders say that their country could strengthen the southern flank of the Atlantic Alliance.

The Romanian peacekeepers will be deployed within the next 10 days on a mission which Degeratu said was aimed "to protect humanitarian aid convoys, and, if need be, to separate (rival) military forces" in Albania.
In January 1993 Romania was the first East European country to sign up for NATO's Partnership for Peace scheme aimed at forging closer military ties with former Cold War foes.
The military has spearheaded Bucharest's post-communist policy efforts to integrate into Western security structures.

Degeratu -- appointed army chief of staff after the centrists removed ex-communists from office for the first time in seven years during elections last November -- said the Albania mission was expected to last six months.

The Romanians will join an effort led by Italy, including southern NATO members France, Greece, Spain, Portugal and Turkey, who are assembling an armed mission for Albania expected to number 2,500 troops and police.

Bucharest is lobbying hard to be invited, along with Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary, for talks on NATO membership when the alliance announces its first eastward expansion at a summit in Madrid in July.
